body:
The parent issue with description is #2690 

Proposed level changes for requirement in chapter "V51 OAuth and OIDC"

Full list of requirements for the chapter is listed here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x51-V51-OAuth2.md

Edit: note that based on discussion, proposed changes were not made.

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **51.4.16** | [ADDED] Verify that if the authorization server supports unauthenticated dynamic client registration, it mitigates the risk of malicious client applications. It must validate client metadata such as any registered URIs, ensure the user's consent and warn the user before processing an authorization request with an untrusted client application. | 2 > 3 |
| **51.7.3** | [ADDED] Verify that the user can review, modify and revoke consents which the user has granted through the authorization server. | 2 > 3 |

comments.body: ping @TobiasAhnoff @randomstuff - compared to previous, 2 more changes.

51.7.3 is one of the most basic and critical controls for OAuth2. We want users to maintain control of this delegated access. I suggest bumping it to L1.

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **51.7.3** | [ADDED] Verify that the user can review, modify and revoke consents which the user has granted through the authorization server. | 2 > 3 |

Note, that consent management has other requirements, that are marked as L2.
* V51.7.1 Verify that the authorization server ensures that the user consents to each authorization request. If the identity of the client cannot be assured, the authorization server must always explicitly prompt the user for consent.	2
* V51.7.2 Verify that when the authorization server prompts for user consent, it presents sufficient and clear information about what is being consented to. When applicable this should include the nature of the requested authorizations (typically based on scope, resource server, Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) authorization details), the identity of the authorized application and the lifetime of these authorizations.

So the current logic is that asking user-consent is L2, management consents is L3. I find that it is too much to ask concent management for "basic security".

Also note, that you ask consent management for L1 and session management for L3 (https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2692#issuecomment-2725972295).

> Also note, that you ask consent management for L1 and session management for L3

This is not completely true. I was suggesting idle timeout be L1 and absolute session and "kill session" be level L2 or L3. 

There is a big different here. Idle timeout automatically closes the session without the user being involved.

With OAuth2, the refresh token is typically long lived or permanent (I have an OAuth2 mobile token for twitter still active since 2011)  and there is no idle timeout. So the only way to cancel that connection is for the user to revoke consent. Without this capabliity, OAuth2 connections are often like true love - forever - without any ability for the user to revoke. That is why I suggest L1 - but only for revoke capabilities.
I maintain my argument for 51.4.16 from https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2673#issue-2898452265 :) I think this is really important and is "expected basic security" (L2).

> With OAuth2, the refresh token is typically long lived or permanent (I have an OAuth2 mobile token for twitter still active since 2011) and there is no idle timeout. So the only way to cancel that connection is for the user to revoke consent.

This is actually partially covered by:

> 51.4.14 [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 3.5.1] Verify that refresh tokens and reference access tokens can be revoked by an authorized user. It can be achieved by using the authorization server user interface, or by a client that is using authorization server APIs for revocation. (L2).

(Note: I still think that "or by a client" should be removed from this requirement).

The difference between 51.4.14 and 51.7.3 is not very clear (and I'm certainly responsible for this).

The idea of the "revoke consent" was intended to be about the ability to revoke the fact that the AS could skip the consent screen for some application. If an application can skip the AS consent screen and this cannot be revoked, it can obtain new access tokens (as long as the user interacts with the application). So it's slightly better than not being able to revoke the access/refresh tokens but not much. I think it should be L2.

> (Note: I still think that "or by a client" should be removed from this requirement).

I agree. If this has not already been debated throughly, consider opening a new issue!
@tghosth - do we skip both proposals here?
I'm not strongly opinionated on V51 so happy to skip for now and leave them as they area.
Ack, those were on the "not sure land" for me as well, so it easy decision to make no action here.
